label: first input step (for 18 of 30 tokens), plus second copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires at two fixed positions. (1) Step t=0, i.e. the very first original token, but only when it is one of 18 tokens: a b c h i j l n q r t v x y z 0 1 2. It never fires at t=0 on d e f g k m o p s u w 3. Since the hidden state is fixed at t=0 the activation depends only on the token: v is highest (about 0.22 of max), then 2, 1, j, y, with b and x near threshold (about 0.02). This part carries about 90% of activation mass. (2) Step t=4 in length-3 sequences (copy phase, recall_idx 1, where the input is the echoed first token). It fires there almost always, whatever the token, and these are the largest activations (up to the max, about 0.85 to 1.0 of max in the top examples). It never fires on the delimiter, on any other original-phase position, or on copy steps for L>3. Dev P=0.999 R=1.0.

issues: Minor: 45 test (35 dev) false positives at L=3, t=4 involve assorted echoed tokens. They look like scattered noise rather than a separate class, about 1.4% of L=3 t=4 steps.

Minor wording: x at t=0 is 0.03 of max, not 0.02, though it is still just above threshold. The claim that t=4 activations are the largest holds per step: mean t=4 activation is about 2.6x the mean at t=0, and the top examples range from 0.85 to 1.0.
